subject: Q4 capacity uplift — reconcile MSA Exhibit E + order addendum
messages:
From: Avery Cloud <avery@blueharbor.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: maria@blueharbor.com, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: 2027-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity uplift + term alignment for Q4

Hi Ben,

Quick context: BlueHarbor is planning a mid-Q4 upsell — we expect to increase committed throughput by ~2.5x and want the renewal terms to reflect a 24-month committed term. Procurement asked us to get the order form and the MSA exhibit aligned before they can route the PO.

Can you help by: 
- Sending the proposed order addendum that shows new tiers and committed units
- Confirming how Exhibit E (usage tiers / overage pricing) will change if we roll into a longer term
- Providing the SOC2 attestation summary and any audit log retention details we can share with procurement

Attached is an internal procurement checklist they asked us to fill out. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Cloud
Finance & Procurement, BlueHarbor Analytics

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Avery Cloud <avery@blueharbor.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-07T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + term alignment for Q4

Hi Avery — thanks for the clear ask.

I put together a quick mutual action plan: 
1) I will attach an updated order form draft showing the 2.5x tiered commit and proposed monthly billing estimate (see attachment: BlueHarbor_Requested_Order_Form_v2.xlsx).
2) Laura will circulate a redline to Exhibit E that clarifies tier thresholds, overage unit pricing, and a pro-rated ramp for the first 30 days.
3) Markus/Legal to confirm the 24-month term language and any auto-renew opt-out notice windows.
4) We will include SOC2 attestation summary and retention notes (SOC2_attestation_summary.pdf) for procurement.

Proposed timeline: Drafts to you by EOD today, we ask procurement to review within 48 hours, sign within the following week. If procurement prefers, we can send Exhibit E as a standalone addendum to avoid re-issuing the entire MSA.

Two quick questions for procurement: are there any specific export/control clauses or data residency obligations we should flag for the legal redline?

Looping in Laura and Markus for redlines and Kimberly from Customer Success to help with usage forecasts that feed the order.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, Avery Cloud <avery@blueharbor.com>
Date: 2027-11-07T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + term alignment for Q4

Ben / Avery — attaching a targeted redline for Exhibit E (MSA_ExhibitE_redline_20271107.pdf). Summary of the edits: 
- Clarified definition of "Committed Units" and added a ramp schedule (Section 2.1).
- Overage pricing: added three-tier bucket pricing with explicit per-unit rates after the commit.
- Term and renewal: added language to allow a customer-requested non-renewal notice window of 60 days before renewal rather than 30, as a concession for the 24-month deal.
- Billing/proration: clarified proration for partial months during the ramp period.

We intentionally kept edits limited to Exhibit E to prevent touching older negotiated MSA clauses. If BlueHarbor requires changes to indemnities or data residency clauses, we will need a separate legal run and likely a countersign timeline extension.

Attachment: MSA_ExhibitE_redline_20271107.pdf (redline comments inline).

Thanks — I recommend we deliver the redline + order form together and ask procurement to flag any hard blockers within 48 hours.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria@blueharbor.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Avery Cloud <avery@blueharbor.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: 2027-11-07T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + term alignment for Q4

Thanks Laura and Ben. A few procurement/legal clarifications from our side: 
- We need confirmation that audit logs (system access / API request logs) are retained for at least 12 months and can be exported on request for internal auditors.
- Any change to data residency (if you plan to route traffic through new regions) must be documented; currently we require EU data for EU customers.
- On the 60-day non-renewal clause: procurement will accept it if you add a one-time migration assistance credit in the event BlueHarbor elects not to renew at term end (amount TBD).

We will review the redline and order form when you send them. If you can include the SOC2 summary and a stub of the audit-log export schema, that would accelerate our internal review.

Best,
Maria Gonzalez
Sr. Procurement Manager, BlueHarbor Analytics
procurement@blueharbor.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria@blueharbor.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-07T16:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + term alignment for Q4

Maria — great notes, thank you. Next steps from Redwood: 
- I attached the updated order form (BlueHarbor_Requested_Order_Form_v2.xlsx) and Laura's Exhibit E redline.
- SOC2_attestation_summary.pdf included; Kimberly will follow up with the audit-log export schema and a short note on retention mechanics.
- On migration assistance: Ben (me) proposes a standard 3-month credit equivalent to X% of committed spend as a one-time fallback; Laura/Markus, please confirm if that's acceptable to add as a contract note for conditional non-renewal.

Can we aim to have procurement signal any legal hard-stops by EOD Thursday so we can spin a DocuSign envelope by next Monday? Putting a tentative DocuSign link below once legal confirms the final redline.

DocuSign preview (will send final after signoff): https://www.docusign.com/Signing?envelopeId=0a1b2c
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Best,
